issues.t: Cruise control deactivation switch can catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell from the engine bay near the brake master cylinder, sometimes even with the truck parked and turned off.
issues.why: A pressure switch for the cruise control mounted on the brake system can leak brake fluid into its electrical side, overheat and start a fire. Ford recalled these trucks to disconnect or fuse the switch.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls right away. Until the recall work is done, park outside and away from buildings.

issues.t: Spark plug blows out of the cylinder head
issues.sym: A sudden loud pop from the engine, then a ticking or puffing sound, rough running, misfire and a check engine light. The ignition coil may be pushed up or broken.
issues.why: The aluminum cylinder heads on these engines hold the spark plugs with only a few threads. Over time the threads can strip and cylinder pressure pushes the plug out.
issues.next: Stop driving and have it towed or repaired soon. The head threads usually need a thread insert or a head replacement; a shop should check the other plugs are tight.

issues.t: Spark plugs seize and break during removal
issues.sym: Misfire or check engine light when plugs are due, and a shop warning that plugs may break or have broken off in the head during a tune-up.
issues.why: The original two-piece plug design lets carbon build up on the lower shell so it sticks in the head and snaps when unscrewed. Ford issued service bulletins with a special removal procedure and tool, and a revised plug.
issues.next: Have plugs replaced by a shop that knows this engine and uses Ford's removal procedure. Insist on the correct plug type to avoid spark knock.

issues.t: Cam phaser and timing chain rattle
issues.sym: A ticking or diesel-like knock from the top of the engine, worst at idle or on a cold start, with rough idle, lost power and cam timing codes.
issues.why: The variable cam timing phasers, their oil-fed solenoids and the chain tensioners and guides wear, especially with low oil pressure or skipped oil changes. Worn parts let timing slip.
issues.next: Have the cause diagnosed soon rather than driving on it, since broken guides or a jumped chain can wreck the engine. Use the specified oil and change it on time.

issues.t: Transmission may suddenly downshift into first gear (recall)
issues.sym: A sudden hard downshift while moving, the rear wheels briefly locking or skidding, and a lurch that can make the truck hard to control.
issues.why: A transmission speed sensor signal can drop out for a moment, and the computer reacts by commanding first gear at speed. Ford recalled these trucks for a software update.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get the free software update before driving much more. If it happens, steer straight and slow down gently.

issues.t: EcoBoost stumble or power loss in damp weather
issues.sym: Shaking, misfire or a sudden loss of power when accelerating hard or towing on humid or rainy days, sometimes with the engine going into reduced-power mode.
issues.why: Water condenses inside the intercooler and gets pulled into the engine in a gulp under boost. Ford released service bulletins adding a deflector and updated engine software, and NHTSA opened an investigation.
issues.next: Ask a Ford dealer whether the intercooler and software updates have been done on your truck.

issues.t: Side doors may not latch or may open while driving (recall)
issues.sym: A door that won't stay shut, a door-ajar warning that won't clear, or a door that pops open while driving.
issues.why: A small spring part inside the side door latch can break, so the latch does not hold properly. Ford recalled these trucks to inspect and replace the latches.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If a door won't latch firmly, don't carry passengers on that side until it is repaired.

issues.t: Seat belt pretensioners can start a fire in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning ahead of time. After a collision that fires the seat belt pretensioners, smoke or flames may appear near the bottom of the door pillars.
issues.why: When the front seat belt pretensioners fire they can throw off strong sparks that ignite nearby insulation and carpet. Ford recalled Regular Cab and SuperCrew trucks to add heat-resistant protection.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the free repair done.

issues.t: Cam phaser rattle on cold start
issues.sym: A loud rattle or clatter for a few seconds after starting a cold engine, sometimes with a check engine light for cam timing.
issues.why: The cam phasers can lose their locked position while the engine sits, so they rattle until oil pressure builds. Ford issued service bulletins and a coverage program for phaser replacement.
issues.next: Have a Ford dealer check whether your truck qualifies for the cam phaser program before paying for the repair.

issues.t: 10-speed automatic harsh or erratic shifting
issues.sym: Hard or clunky shifts, slipping, delayed engagement, or the truck hunting between gears, especially at low speed.
issues.why: Owners have reported rough shifting on the 10-speed automatic, and class action lawsuits were filed over it. Many cases improve with updated software and a relearn; some need internal repairs.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to check for updated transmission software and perform an adaptive relearn first, and keep records of every visit.
issues.eng: Engines paired with the 10-speed automatic (3.5L and 2.7L EcoBoost, 5.0L V8, 3.0L diesel)

issues.t: Excessive oil consumption
issues.sym: Oil level dropping fast between changes, a low-oil warning, blue smoke on startup, or misfires from fouled plugs.
issues.why: Oil gets past the piston rings and is burned in the cylinders. Ford issued a service bulletin covering oil consumption on these engines, and owners filed lawsuits over it.
issues.next: Check the oil level every fill-up and top up as needed. If it uses a lot, ask a dealer for an oil consumption test under the bulletin.

issues.t: Parking brake may apply by itself (recall)
issues.sym: A brake warning light, and the parking brake engaging on its own, sometimes while driving.
issues.why: The wiring harness on the rear axle can rub on the axle housing until the wires short, which can trigger the electric parking brake. Ford recalled these trucks to protect or replace the harness.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get it repaired promptly. If the brake warning light comes on, have the truck inspected before regular driving.

issues.t: Windshield wiper motor may stop working (recall)
issues.sym: Front wipers that work only some of the time or stop completely.
issues.why: The front wiper motor can fail. Ford recalled affected trucks to replace the motor.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Do not drive in rain or snow with wipers that are acting up.

issues.t: Rear axle hub bolt can break (recall)
issues.sym: Loss of drive power, clunking from the rear, or the truck rolling while in Park if the parking brake isn't set.
issues.why: On trucks with the Max Trailer Tow package and heavy-duty rear axle, the bolt holding the axle hub can fatigue and break, damaging the splines that drive the wheel. Ford recalled these trucks to replace both rear axle shafts.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Always set the parking brake when parked until the repair is done, and stop towing if the rear end makes noise.

issues.t: Camera menu can cover the backup camera image (recall)
issues.sym: When shifting into Reverse, a camera-views menu stays on the center screen and partly blocks the rear camera picture.
issues.why: Infotainment software on trucks with the 8-inch screen does not always close the camera menu when Reverse is selected. Ford is updating the software over the air or at a dealer.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and accept the software update. Close the menu by hand and use your mirrors until then.

issues.t: Inside door handle spring can break (recall)
issues.sym: An inside door handle feels loose or does not spring back after you pull it.
issues.why: A spring in the inside door handle can break. With the handle not returning fully, the door may not stay latched in a side crash. Ford recalled these trucks to inspect and repair the handles.
issues.next: Have a Ford dealer run your VIN for this recall. If a handle feels loose, get it looked at soon.

issues.t: Brake light switch may be out of adjustment (recall)
issues.sym: The brake lights may stay on when your foot is off the pedal, or may not come on when you brake.
issues.why: The stop lamp switch at the brake pedal may not have been adjusted correctly at the factory. Ford recalled affected trucks to check and reset it.
issues.next: Ask someone to watch the brake lights while you press and release the pedal, and have a dealer check your VIN for this recall.

issues.t: Timing chain stretch
issues.sym: Check engine light, often with a short rattle from the front of the engine on a cold start.
issues.why: The main timing chain on the early 3.5L EcoBoost can wear and lengthen, which throws cam timing off enough to set a code. Ford issued a service bulletin with an updated chain kit.
issues.next: Have the code read and the chain checked before long. Keeping up with oil changes helps slow the wear.

issues.t: Brake master cylinder can leak fluid (recall)
issues.sym: Red brake warning light, low brake fluid with no puddle under the truck, and a brake pedal that sinks or needs more effort.
issues.why: The master cylinder on trucks with the 3.5L EcoBoost can leak brake fluid into the brake booster. That takes away braking from the front wheels. Ford recalled these trucks in two campaigns.
issues.next: Do not ignore a brake warning light or a soft pedal. Have the truck checked right away and confirm the recall work was done.

issues.t: Oil pan seal leak
issues.sym: Oil drips under the engine or an oily film on the bottom of the oil pan.
issues.why: The sealant between the plastic oil pan and the engine can let go on the 2.7L EcoBoost. Ford issued a service bulletin calling for a new, revised pan.
issues.next: Check the oil level regularly and have the leak confirmed and repaired at your next visit.

issues.t: Intake valves can break (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden misfire, loss of power or an engine that quits and will not restart.
issues.why: Intake valves in some 2.7L EcoBoost engines were made from a material that can crack and break. A broken valve can wreck the engine. Ford recalled affected trucks after a federal investigation.
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN for this recall. If the engine starts running rough or loses power, stop driving and have it towed.

issues.t: Backup camera image can freeze or go blank (recall)
issues.sym: The screen shows a frozen, delayed or blank picture when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: A software fault in the screen module can stop the rear camera image from showing correctly. Ford recalled these trucks for a software update that can be done at the dealer or over the air.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and get the update. Until then, use your mirrors and look behind you when backing up.

issues.t: Trailer brake and lights can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: Trailer warning messages on the dash, or trailer brakes and turn signals that quit while towing.
issues.why: The built-in trailer module can lose communication with the truck. Ford recalled these trucks for a software update.
issues.next: If you tow, have the recall update done before your next trip and check the trailer lights and brakes each time you hook up.

issues.t: Fuel tank straps may not hold the tank (recall)
issues.sym: Fuel smell, fuel dripping under the truck, or a tank that hangs low or rattles.
issues.why: The straps that hold the fuel tank may not be secured properly. The tank can shift, leak or come loose. Ford recalled these trucks to inspect and replace the straps.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. If you smell fuel or see the tank sagging, stop driving and have the truck towed in.

issues.t: Engine oil plug can leak quickly (recall)
issues.sym: Oil warning light, a large oil leak under the engine, or a burning-oil smell.
issues.why: A sealing plug in the 3.5L turbo engine may have been pressed in crooked. It can let oil out fast, which can damage the engine or start a fire if oil reaches hot parts. Ford recalled affected trucks to inspect and replace the plug.
issues.next: If the oil light comes on or you see a big leak, shut the engine off and have the truck towed. Check your VIN for this recall.

issues.t: Transmission valve body fault can cause loss of reverse (recall)
issues.sym: Reverse does not engage, or the truck moves in a direction you did not expect.
issues.why: The valve body inside the automatic transmission may have been machined incorrectly. Ford recalled affected trucks to replace it.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. If reverse acts up or the truck moves unexpectedly, park it and call the dealer.

issues.t: Steering gear can bind or lock (recall)
issues.sym: Steering that feels notchy, sticks or becomes very hard to turn.
issues.why: Some steering gears were built with the wrong rack, which can crack the gear teeth inside. Ford recalled affected trucks to replace the steering gear.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. If the steering binds or feels wrong, do not drive the truck until it is inspected.

issues.t: Windshield may not be bonded properly (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you can see. Some owners may notice wind noise or a water leak around the glass.
issues.why: The windshield adhesive may not have bonded correctly at the factory, so the glass could come out in a crash. Ford recalled affected trucks to remove and reinstall the windshield.
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN for this recall and get the windshield rebonded.
